sources.excerpt: Kylian Mbappe ends long-term Nike partnership to lead On’s football boots expansion. Real Madrid striker Kylian Mbappe has quit his long-term relationship with Nike to become the face of Swiss company On’s first expansion into football boots. On has long been associated with premium running shoes and previously expanded into tennis. Roger Federer joined in a deal in 2019 which saw him receive equity, while athletes who now wear On’s apparel and shoes include U.S. Open finalist Ben Shelton. On’s venture into football, however, arguably represents the boldest move of the 17-year-old Swiss company’s history. As part of its expansion, it has also hired former France and Arsenal star Thierry Henry as the firm’s Director of Football. Henry has been secretly working in the role since 2025 and played a role in convincing Mbappe, 27, to join upon the expiration of his contract with Nike this summer. In doing so, the France international has shunned not only Nike but also leading footwear brands such as Adidas and Puma, while there is now a new rival for relative upstarts New Balance and Skechers on the market. The financial terms of the deal have not been disclosed, but The Athletic can also reveal that Mbappe has been given equity in the Swiss company. On declined to comment. In a statement on Friday, On said that Mbappe “will be at the heart of On’s football journey, uniting one of football’s defining players with one of sportswear’s most innovative brands.” They added: “He will work directly with On’s product teams, integrating his elite perspective into the development and testing of future football footwear and apparel. He will also become a global ambassador for On, extending the partnership beyond football into movement, performance and contemporary design.” Mbappe said: “From the beginning, what drew me to On was the opportunity to build something entirely new together that will help shape tomorrow’s game, I want to bring my experience and perspective into what we create, push what’s possible through innovation, and always stay true to the joy of football. We have a shared dream, and this is only the beginning.” Mbappe is also set to appear in On boots on EA Sports FC 2027, which is officially released worldwide on September 25. On also announced an extension of an existing partnership with Swiss international and Barcelona player Sydney Schertenleib. She joined On in December 2025 as an ambassador for training and lifestyle apparel but will now also work on football boots.On founder David Allemann told The Athletic that their boots will hit the retail market in 2027 and will be “premium” products. The company is also looking to make a splash in the women’s market ahead of the FIFA Women’s World Cup next summer, but Mbappe is expected to be seen on the field in his new boots over the coming weeks. Mbappe’s departure from Nike is symbolic of a trend among leading athletes who appear to crave greater input and ownership of their relationship with a brand. Mbappe had been with Nike since 2006, when he was only nine-years-old. It has been a highly lucrative relationship and Nike committed to him at a time when they shed relationships with many players in order to consolidate around a small number of high profile talent such as Mbappe, Cristiano Ronaldo and Erling Haaland. Nike told The Athletic: “Kylian’s journey with Nike began when he was nine years old. Over nearly two decades, we’ve shared moments that shaped the game and he has been an important part of Nike Football. We are proud of what we achieved together on and off the pitch. As he moves into the next phase of his career, we wish him continued success for what comes next.” But Mbappe appears to have been tempted by the opportunity to distinguish himself by becoming the undisputed face of a new football boot brand at On. “Football doesn’t need another sportswear brand to do more of the same,” added Allemann. “Football needs new ideas and a challenge to what is possible. When we enter a sport, we want to be the brand of the future – through true innovation and contemporary design. With Kylian we have the perfect partner to dream what football can become.”

Kylian Mbappé leaves Nike after 20 years to sign boot deal with Swiss brand On. Kylian Mbappé has ended a 20-year association with Nike to sign a boot deal with the Swiss challenger company On. The sports and leisure brand, which has previously focused on running and tennis, is planning a major move into football next year and has also appointed Thierry Henry as its football director. Roger Federer, who also left Nike to join them towards the end of his playing career, is a shareholder of the Zurich-based company. Mbappé will also become a shareholder in On. “From the beginning, what drew me to On was the opportunity to build something entirely new together that will help shape tomorrow’s game,” said the France captain. “I want to bring my experience and perspective into what we create, push what’s possible through innovation, and always stay true to the joy of football. We have a shared dream, and this is only the beginning.” On is a newcomer to football and this week unveiled its first boots, the Lightspray Prototype, which will be available for the mass market from next year before a move into training kit. Mbappé’s departure, which came at the end of his contract after the World Cup, is a significant blow for Nike, which also lost the Barcelona and Spain star Lamine Yamal to Adidas two years ago. The 27-year-old has been the face of many of Nike’s advertising campaigns. “Kylian’s journey with Nike began when he was nine years old,” the company said in a statement. “Over nearly two decades, we’ve shared moments that shaped the game and he has been an important part of Nike Football. We are proud of what we achieved together on and off the pitch.” Nike and Adidas dominate the football market with their boots worn by more than 40% of players at this summer’s World Cup, according to data compiled by the retailer Fútbol Emotion, with Puma accounting for about 10%.

Kylian Mbappé leaves Nike and signs with sponsor On. Kylian Mbappé has signed with sportswear brand On after leaving Nike. Nike had previously sponsored Mbappé since he was a child, and the Real Madrid forward wore their Mercurial boots, but he is now set for a significant change. Swiss brand On, who began in 2010 as a running shoe manufacturer then added tennis legend Roger Federer as a co-owner in 2019, are entering the football market and have also announced Thierry Henry will be their director of football. Mbappé, who will also become a global ambassador for his new sponsor, "will work directly with On's product teams," an On statement read. Mbappé said: "From the beginning, what drew me to On was the opportunity to build something entirely new together that will help shape tomorrow's game. I want to bring my experience and perspective into what we create, push what's possible through innovation, and always stay true to the joy of football. We have a shared dream, and this is only the beginning." David Allemann, founder and co-CEO of On, said: "Football doesn't need another sportswear brand to do more of the same. Football needs new ideas and a challenge to what is possible. When we enter a sport, we want to be the brand of the future -- through true innovation and contemporary design. Our ambition is to bring On's approach to the pitch, the pavement, and the runway -- connecting elite performance with the culture that surrounds the game. With Kylian we have the perfect partner to dream what football can become." Ex-France, Barcelona and Arsenal striker Henry said: "Building something new in football requires a bold and original approach. Over the past year, I've seen first-hand the curiosity and attention to detail the team at On brings to that process. We want to listen to players, understand what they need and create something that can genuinely add to the game. I'm proud to be part of shaping what comes next." Sydney Schertenleib, who has worked with On since 2025 but will now work in product development and testing of their football entry, said: "I've already experienced how differently On thinks about performance and design, so being part of its journey into football feels really exciting. As a player, having the opportunity to work directly with On and bring my perspective into the development process is something really special. I can honestly say, I've never felt the ball like I have in the product the team is working on." A statement on social media from Mbappé read: "Dream On, Football. I still dream of playing football. That might surprise you, coming from someone who plays it for a living. But it's true. I still dream of playing with my friends. Playing until sunset. Until dinner. Playing just because it was a game, long before it could become a career. "I have followed this dream for as long as I can remember. Once again it has led me to one of the biggest changes in my life. Of bringing the people as close as possible to the game. Of bringing the world as close as possible to play. "I guess that's the thing about dreams that refuse to change. "They're usually the ones that change everything. Dream On." Mbappé's exit from Nike follows Lamine Yamal, who left the brand to sign with new sponsor Adidas.
